close_reason: Delivered in PR #303 (audited 2026-09-06: logs/<current|old>/<log_id> family written by recovery, Exclusion.check_logs/2 reader, 20+ tests). Residuals tracked separately: stale-master spike is bedrock-q67.53, logs/old pruning is bedrock-q67.54. Stacked on #299, no CI run.
description:
Recorded so a real insight from the bedrock-q67.21.10 audit is not lost: 'no readers' can mean 'the readers are not built yet'. For layout/logs it did not (see WHY THE DELETED FAMILY DOES NOT COME BACK), but the FUTURE readers FDB has are ones Bedrock will plausibly want, and this ticket captures what they actually require.

FDB keeps \xff/logs (SystemData.cpp:1171), written by the recovery transaction (ClusterRecovery.actor.cpp:1728). Payload, from TagPartitionedLogSystem::getLogsValue (TagPartitionedLogSystem.actor.cpp:1831-1854): a vector of (UID, NetworkAddress) for the CURRENT log servers, plus a second vector for OLD generations while recoveryComplete has not been written to core state.

THE READERS AND WHAT THEY CONSUME:
1. Exclusion safety — checkForExcludingServersTxActor (ManagementAPI.actor.cpp:2393-2408). Reads logsKey and, for both current and old generations, fails the safety check if a log's address is excluded OR is the empty NetworkAddress. This is what makes 'exclude a node' safe: you cannot exclude a machine still hosting a log needed for recovery. It needs ADDRESSES and it needs OLD GENERATIONS.
2. In-progress-exclusion special key module (SpecialKeySpace.actor.cpp:1294) — same feature family, surfaced through the special key space.
3. Recovery's stale-master fence — updateLogsValue (ClusterRecovery.actor.cpp:770-801): reads logsKey, decodes the log ids, and returns early if none intersect the current logSystem's tLogs, with CODE_PROBE 'old master attempted to change logsKey'. A keyspace-mediated guard against a superseded master mutating shared state.

WHY THE DELETED FAMILY DOES NOT COME BACK: layout/logs stored log_id -> [shard_tag]. No addresses, no old generations. It could not have answered any of the three questions above. When exclusion arrives it needs a NEW family shaped like FDB's, and reviving a tag-list family would have been worse than deleting it — a record that looks like infrastructure while being unable to answer the question its readers ask.

SCOPE WHEN PICKED UP: this is really the keyspace half of an EXCLUSION feature (operational node removal), which Bedrock does not have at all. Do not build the family speculatively — build it with its first reader, per the project convention. The value here is knowing the shape in advance: addresses, current AND prior generations, written by the recovery transaction.

ALSO WORTH SETTLING (smaller, independent): does Bedrock have FDB's stale-master hazard at all? Our director commits its system transaction through its own epoch's commit proxies, and the next epoch's recovery locks every log and materializer at the new epoch — so a superseded director's commit should be rejected at the log/materializer layer rather than needing a keyspace fence. That is a plausible argument, NOT a verified one. Confirm it with a falsifiable spike (drive a superseded director's persistence commit against services locked at a newer epoch and observe the rejection) before concluding we need no equivalent of updateLogsValue. If the hazard IS real, the fence belongs with reader 3 above.

comments.text: Draft PR: https://github.com/bedrock-kv/bedrock/pull/303 — \xFF/system/logs/<generation>/<log_id> -> node written by LogRecruitmentPhase into pending_tx (current + survivors), read by Bedrock.ControlPlane.Exclusion.check_logs/2. Stacked on #299. Cold audit PASS-WITH-NOTES, all findings addressed. Follow-ups worth tickets: (1) logs/old/ is never pruned (FDB's updateLogsValue) — needs a durability watcher clearing it once the object-storage durable version passes the recovery version; over-refuses in the safe direction until then. (2) The storage half of FDB's exclusion check (materializers/) is deliberately absent — it needs data movement (q67.46) to have a path to safety, which is why the verdict is :no_log_blockers and not :safe. (3) The operator surface (\xff/conf/excluded/ + command) is unbuilt; the reader's only caller today is the test suite. The ticket's second half — whether Bedrock has FDB's stale-master hazard at all (updateLogsValue's fence) — was NOT settled here; it still wants the falsifiable spike the ticket describes.

title: Exclusion safety needs a keyspace log record: addresses and OLD generations, not tag lists
